title: The Day the Ground Shook
text:
Last summer, a strong earthquake shook the small town of Rivera. Many buildings were damaged, and some roads were closed. Luckily, the people in the town knew what to do because the school had practised safety drills.

After the earthquake, volunteers from nearby cities came to help. They gave water and food to families who had lost their homes. Within a week, the town started to rebuild its schools and shops.

questions.text: What happened to some roads in Rivera?
What did the volunteers give to the families?
Why did most people in Rivera know what to do during the earthquake?
options: They had practised safety drills at school
They had lived through earthquakes every year
A radio told them the exact time to act
They had read a book about earthquakes

questions.text: What can the reader infer about the future of the town?
options: It will slowly recover from the disaster
It will never receive any help

vocabulary.definition: a sudden shaking of the ground caused by movement under the Earth
harmed or broken so that it does not work well
people who help others without being paid
to build again after something has been destroyed

paragraph_translations: El verano pasado, un fuerte terremoto sacudió el pequeño pueblo de Rivera. Muchos edificios resultaron dañados y algunas carreteras fueron cerradas. Por suerte, la gente del pueblo sabía qué hacer, porque la escuela había practicado simulacros de seguridad.

Después del terremoto, llegaron voluntarios de las ciudades cercanas para ayudar. Entregaron agua y comida a las familias que habían perdido sus casas. En una semana, el pueblo empezó a reconstruir sus escuelas y tiendas.
